title: Random matrix images of a nonzero vector are uniform
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite field, and fix $n \ge 0$ and $k \ge 1$. Let $x \in \alpha^k$ be a nonzero vector. Then the distribution on $\alpha^n$ obtained by sampling an $n \times k$ matrix $G$ with entries in $\alpha$ uniformly at random and returning the product $Gx$ coincides with the uniform distribution on $\alpha^n$; that is, for every $v \in \alpha^n$,
\[
\frac{\bigl|\{\,G \in \alpha^{n \times k} : Gx = v\,\}\bigr|}{\abs{\alpha}^{nk}} = \frac{1}{\abs{\alpha}^{n}}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: x is a nonzero codeword of length k
equality of the two distributions holds at every v in alpha^n
replaced:
If $x\neq 0$ and $k\ge 1$, then for a uniformly random $n\times k$ matrix $G$ over $\alpha$,
the product $Gx$ is uniformly distributed over $\alpha^n$:
\[
\Pr[Gx = v] = \frac{1}{|\alpha|^n}
\quad\text{for all }v\in\alpha^n.
\]
